is_anopheles.evidence: Section 2.1 (page 2): 'The mosquitoes used in this study were Anopheles gambiae (s.s.), originating from Busia, Uganda.'

reports_target_markers.evidence: The authors do not genotype any mosquitoes in this study. They only mention in Section 2.1 (page 2) that the colony strain has known mechanisms described in previous literature: 'The strain is resistant to pyrethroids, with alterations in the target site (Vgsc-1014S) and metabolic resistance mechanisms (Cyp4j5, Cyp6aa1, and Coea1d) (Weetman et al., 2018; Njoroge et al., 2021; Mechan et al., 2022).'

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype or allele counts/frequencies are generated or reported in this study.

african_field_population.evidence: Section 2.1 (page 2): Tests were performed solely using an insectary colony established in November 2018 and maintained at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine under deltamethrin selection every five generations.

is_primary_study.evidence: Primary laboratory behavioral study using modified cone bioassays.

sub_country_location.evidence: Section 2.1 (page 2): The colony originally came from Busia, Uganda.

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Section 2.1 (page 2): Original colony collection date was November 2018.

duplicate_risk.evidence: Not applicable; no new genotype data reported.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated behavioral responses (movement and net contact) and mortality of a pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae colony (Busia strain) exposed to bednets (PermaNet 2.0, PermaNet 3.0, Olyset, Olyset Plus) of various post-deployment ages using a video cone bioassay. No genotyping of insecticide resistance markers was performed.
exclusion_reasons: No target insecticide resistance markers were genotyped in this study.
No extractable genotype frequency or count data reported.
Tested mosquitoes were from a long-term laboratory colony maintained at LSTM rather than field-collected mosquitoes or F1 progeny.
